summary: The curated subset presents strong fail-closed scanning, artifact validation, execution approval, credential minimization, and independent verification contracts. Medium gaps remain in the scanner's documented runtime prerequisites and consistent recognition of supported JavaScript/TypeScript configuration extensions and loopback fallback hosts.

findings.title: Undocumented mandatory Python dependency
findings.evidence: Candidate fingerprinting returns failure when no bound Python 3 executable exists, and the mandatory manifest-recording path converts that failure into exit 2. This conflicts with the included public guidance that identifies PCRE2-capable ripgrep as the bundled scanner requirement and describes Python only for optional Tier 2 validation.
findings.recommendation: Document Python 3 as a mandatory Tier 3 scanner prerequisite, or implement the candidate-identity baseline without requiring Python and retain Python only for optional tiers.

findings.title: Framework detection narrows the shared extension scope
findings.evidence: Phase 0 instructs reviewers to inspect actual imports only in `.ts` and `.js` files, while the included scanner and generator contracts support `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.mts`, `.mjs`, `.cts`, and `.cjs` as well. A suite using those forms can therefore be misclassified before framework-specific checks run.
findings.recommendation: Use the same eight-extension set for Phase 0 framework detection and state it once as a shared contract.

findings.title: Playwright diagnosis omits supported config forms
findings.evidence: The required configuration read is limited to `playwright.config.{ts,js}`, despite included public surfaces recognizing additional JavaScript/TypeScript forms. Retry, parallelism, baseURL, timeout, and webServer evidence can consequently be missed for supported configurations.
findings.recommendation: Require discovery of Playwright configuration across the shared supported extension set before F1, F7, or F8 classification.

findings.title: Cypress diagnosis omits supported config forms
findings.evidence: The classification procedure requires only `cypress.config.{js,ts}` even though the included scanner's project boundary recognizes `.mts`, `.mjs`, `.cts`, and `.cjs` Cypress configurations. This can omit retries, isolation, timeout, and baseUrl evidence.
findings.recommendation: Align Cypress configuration discovery with the scanner's complete recognized configuration set.

findings.title: ARIA fallback rejects valid loopback aliases without advance notice
findings.evidence: The fallback accepts only literal `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1` hostnames, although the preceding preflight contract permits an approved hostname whose entire DNS set is loopback. A local alias such as an approved development hostname can pass preflight and then fail only inside the fallback.
findings.recommendation: Either validate the approved DNS snapshot in the fallback and accept all-loopback aliases, or disclose the literal-host restriction before preflight and provide the exact remediation.

limitations: Packet-only static review; no files outside the frozen subset were considered.
No commands, tests, benchmarks, holdouts, network checks, or runtime probes were executed.
Scores assess included contracts and verification design, not observed runtime success, benchmark accuracy, full product coverage, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.
